title: Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers — Extension of the Expiry Date
content:
Reservations and Loyalty desk rule note on extending the expiry date of a credit from Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers.

## Rule in force

1. **Availability.** An active credit may be extended where its instrument permits extension and the credit's extension count is below the instrument's maximum number of extensions.
2. **Request window.** An extension can be requested no earlier than the instrument's number of calendar days before the credit's expiry date as recorded on the credit. The window opens that many calendar days before the expiry date, and a request on the opening day is accepted. The request must be made on or before the expiry date itself. An expired credit is handled by reinstatement instead.
3. **New expiry date.** Adding months to the expiry date keeps the day of the month, and falls back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist. The credit's extension count increases by one.
4. **Fee waiver.** The extension fee is waived where the customer's Summit tier under the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program waives credit service fees. A waived fee is not recorded.
5. **Fee entries.** A credit fee entry is charged only on a credit whose status is active or expired, as the system records it for that credit.
6. **What an extension does not change.** An extension never changes the face value, the traveler name or the traveler scope.

## Clauses no longer in force

- The former clause under which an active credit's expiry date may be extended by the instrument's extension months is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis for the extension term. The availability conditions in rule 1 remain in force.
- The former clause under which the new expiry date is the old expiry date plus the instrument's extension months is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis for the extension term. The month-end fallback and the increase of the extension count in rule 3 remain in force.
- The former clause under which the extension fee is charged as a separate fee entry at the time of the extension is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis for the extension fee. The waiver in rule 4 remains in force.

## Request window, boundary cases (hypothetical, 60-day window)

| Credit expiry date as recorded | Request date | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 30 August 2026 | 30 June 2026 | Too early; the window opens on 1 July 2026 |
| 30 August 2026 | 1 July 2026 (opening day) | Accepted |
| 30 August 2026 | 30 August 2026 (the expiry date) | Accepted |
| 30 August 2026 | 31 August 2026 | The credit is past its expiry date; this is handled by reinstatement |

The expiry date recorded on the credit is the evidence for the window. The customer's own account of the date is not.

superseded_clauses: An active credit's expiry_date may be extended by extension_months calendar months
The new expiry_date is the old expiry_date plus extension_months calendar months
The extension_fee is charged as a separate fee entry at the time of the extension
